“How do you eliminate spike protein? There are really only two effective methods,” explained Dr. Paul Marik.

• The first method is triggering autophagy through intermittent fasting (also known as time-restricted eating). Autophagy functions like your cell’s internal cleanup system, removing damaged components—including spike protein inside the cell.

• The second approach involves taking nattokinase, an enzyme derived from fermented soy.  

“Nattokinase breaks down spike protein in the extracellular space,” Dr. Marik clarified. “If the spike is inside the cell, autophagy is the only way to clear it. But if it’s outside the cell, nattokinase can effectively break it down.”

While each method supports spike clearance, Dr. Marik recommends combining both intermittent fasting and nattokinase for optimal results.

⚠️ Thousands of wallets in the Cardano ecosystem may be at risk

SecondFi (formerly Yoroi) has reportedly suffered a security incident related to wallet generation, potentially exposing users' private keys.

What we know so far:

🔴 Around 16 million ADA ($2.4M) has already been stolen from 374 wallets.
🔴 The platform has suspended its services, entered maintenance mode, and promised to compensate affected users.
🔴 Large transfers totaling 129 million ADA, initially suspected to be theft, were actually executed by SecondFi itself to secure user funds.
🔴 If the issue is indeed caused by predictable private key generation, all wallets created through the vulnerable version of the app could remain at risk.

❗️Most importantly, the team is advising users NOT to move funds to new wallets and NOT to import their seed phrases into other applications. According to the developers, the risk appears to arise during transaction signing itself.

For now, Cardano users should closely follow official updates and avoid taking rushed actions that could make the situation worse. 👀

📌 Token Vesting: Why Team and Investor Tokens Unlock Over Time

Main Points
⏺ Token vesting schedules control when founders, teams, and investors can claim their tokens
⏺ Unlocks are usually spread over months or years with cliffs and linear releases
⏺ This post explains how vesting protects projects from instant dump pressure

1️⃣ What Is Vesting — tokens reserved for insiders are locked and only become claimable at set dates
2️⃣ Cliff Period — an initial lockup (for example, 6–12 months) where no tokens unlock at all
3️⃣ Linear Unlock — after the cliff, tokens are released gradually, such as monthly over several years
4️⃣ Market Impact — large unlocks can increase sell pressure, so traders often track vesting calendars
5️⃣ Trust Signal — transparent vesting shows that core contributors are aligned for the long term, not just a quick exit

Final Thoughts

Token vesting turns insider allocations into a time-based commitment — the longer they’re locked in, the more skin in the game the project really has.

Former Ethereum Foundation developer Trent Van Epps warns that Ethereum could face a funding crisis within the next 3–9 months 

For years, the Ethereum Foundation has followed a “subtraction” strategy—gradually reducing its influence so the network can thrive independently. However, EF still remains a key pillar of legitimacy through its brand, ties to Vitalik Buterin, developer events, and ecosystem coordination.

The bigger issue is funding. After spending much of its ETH reserves on ecosystem growth, EF plans to cut annual spending from 15% to 5% by 2030. Meanwhile, its 4-year Client Incentive Program ended in April 2026 with no replacement announced.

Maintaining client teams, research, and protocol coordination costs around $30M per year. Without a sustainable funding model, Ethereum risks losing experienced developers and slowing progress on scaling, quantum-resistance research, and core network maintenance.

Ethereum’s biggest challenge may not be technology—it may be funding the people building it.

Hormuz: Free Water, Paid Illusions

The Strait of Hormuz just turned into the world’s most expensive “free” lane. Oman proudly tells the International Maritime Organization it has set up a temporary safe route to guarantee freedom of navigation and reminds everyone that maritime law doesn’t allow transit tolls. 

South Korea counts four tankers that made it out, one limping home, while 18 are still stuck. Qatar’s prime minister whispers to the Financial Times that LNG exports will be back “within weeks,” and that he’s ready to play therapist between Iran, the Gulf monarchies and Iraq over reopening the strait. But with the Gulf side pushing hard to kill any talk of fees.

On the surface, markets are already back on their meds. Oil slips to around 75 dollars a barrel, close to pre‑war levels, and Trump orders the Justice Department to investigate oil companies for “gouging” at the pump instead of thanking them for his polling numbers. 

At the same time, he insists Iran has promised no tolls, no insurance surcharges, no extra charges of any kind for crossing Hormuz, and threatens to walk away from talks if it turns out they were lying. 

To make it sound like a patriotic infomercial, he swears the U.S. isn’t giving Iran cash; Washington will just “release” some Iranian money so Tehran can buy desperately needed corn, wheat and soybeans from American farmers.

The part he skips is the one written in fine print in Muscat and Tehran. Iran and Oman now publicly claim Hormuz as part of their territorial waters and have set up a joint framework to decide “costs” and “services” for passage. 

They promise no tolls for 60 days, a cooling‑off period dressed up as a victory tweet, after which the final deal kicks in and the fees become non‑negotiable. 

Europe’s aviation watchdog, meanwhile, waves a red flag over the skies above Iran, Iraq and Lebanon, warning airlines to stay away because a cease‑fire that exists on paper doesn’t stop missiles from mistaking civilian aircraft for radar noise.

🔔 Ripple targets $1B revenue run rate without counting XRP holdings 

❗️ According to posts shared by CoinMarketCap and crypto-focused accounts on X, Ripple expects to end 2026 with a $1 billion revenue run rate. The figure does not include XRP held on Ripple’s balance sheet. That detail matters because Ripple has long faced public debate over the link between its business and XRP. Garlinghouse’s target frames the company as a fintech infrastructure provider that aims to earn money from products, clients, and services, not from token holdings or sales.

🌐 The deal also supports Ripple USD, known as RLUSD. Ripple has promoted the stablecoin for enterprise settlement and collateral use. Recently, crypto news reported that Ripple is also adding RLUSD to new payment tools, including services tied to AI agents and machine payments on the XRP Ledger. Company materials point to custody, treasury management, and liquidity services as core offerings. These products target banks and firms that need faster settlement, account control, and access to digital assets through regulated processes, rather than retail trading.
